summary: Add a local-first TimeSlotRating feature to CyberSchedule RN: users can record a completed time slot with rating, efficiency, optional activity/mood/reflection, persist it locally through a repository abstraction, browse recent history from a new RATING tab, export ratings as JSON from settings, and leave schema/service extension points for future cloud sync without touching existing ScheduleEvent data.

phases.name: Domain Model and Storage Foundation
phases.description: Create the rating feature directory, define the TimeSlotRating type, repository contract, AsyncStorage-backed storage module, and LocalRatingRepository. This phase establishes the local persistence layer and cloud-sync extension points without adding UI.
acceptance: src/features/rating/types.ts defines TimeSlotRating exactly with id, slot_start, slot_end, linked_event_id, rating, efficiency, mood, activity, reflection, created_at, updated_at, synced_at, and schema_version.
src/features/rating/storage/repository.ts exposes the RatingRepository interface with list, get, save, remove, listPendingSync, and markSynced.

src/features/rating/storage/ratings.storage.ts uses AsyncStorage key cs-rn:time-slot-ratings:v1 and follows the existing events.storage.ts pattern: load-on-demand, in-memory cache, CRUD, and listener notifications.
src/features/rating/storage/local-repository.ts implements RatingRepository by wrapping ratings.storage.ts.
Storage preserves rating and efficiency as independent 1-5 values.
Storage writes schema_version: 1, created_at, updated_at, and leaves synced_at undefined/null for unsynced local records.
tests: ratings.storage.test.ts covers empty initial state.
ratings.storage.test.ts covers create then list/get.

ratings.storage.test.ts covers update then list/get, including updated_at refresh behavior if the storage layer is responsible for timestamp refresh; otherwise verify the saved updated_at value is preserved from service input.
ratings.storage.test.ts covers delete then list/get.
ratings.storage.test.ts covers JSON serialize/deserialize edge cases: optional empty fields, emoji, long strings.
ratings.storage.test.ts verifies rating and efficiency are both saved and read correctly.
local-repository.test.ts verifies listPendingSync returns only records whose synced_at is null or undefined.
local-repository.test.ts verifies markSynced removes the record from the pending-sync result.

phases.name: Rating Service and Hook
phases.description: Add the service layer that depends only on RatingRepository, plus a React hook for screens/components to consume ratings. This phase centralizes validation, timestamp handling, default slot creation, and repository injection before UI is introduced.
acceptance: src/features/rating/services/ratings.service.ts performs CRUD through RatingRepository and does not import ratings.storage.ts directly.
Service creates new ratings with uuid id, default slot_start as now minus 1 hour, default slot_end as now, created_at, updated_at, schema_version: 1, and unsynced synced_at.
Service validates/clamps or rejects rating and efficiency outside 1-5.
Service enforces optional field limits: mood <= 20, activity <= 50, reflection <= 200.
Service exposes JSON export data through list or a dedicated export helper without coupling to Share/expo-sharing.
src/features/rating/hooks/useRatings.ts loads ratings, refreshes after save/remove, exposes loading/error state, and subscribes to storage/listener updates if the storage pattern supports listeners.
src/features/rating/index.ts exports public feature APIs needed by app screens.
tests: Unit tests for ratings.service.ts create path: default dates, uuid presence, schema_version, created_at, updated_at, unsynced state.
Unit tests for ratings.service.ts update path: updated_at changes while created_at remains stable.
Unit tests for ratings.service.ts validation: rating and efficiency must be 1-5.
Unit tests for ratings.service.ts field length behavior for mood, activity, and reflection.
Unit tests use a fake RatingRepository to prove the service is repository-based and storage-independent.

phases.name: Core Rating UI Components
phases.description: Build reusable visual components for rating input and history while matching the existing cyberpunk theme conventions. This phase requires reading app/_layout.tsx, app/index.tsx, EventSheet.tsx, src/theme/index.ts, and at least one existing tab page before implementation.
acceptance: src/features/rating/components/StarRating.tsx renders 1-5 interactive stars using theme colors from useTheme, with active fill, inactive outline, press feedback, and no hardcoded colors.
src/features/rating/components/EfficiencySlider.tsx renders a custom themed 1-5 discrete slider with track, active range, thumb, tick marks, and current numeric value in Orbitron.

src/features/rating/components/RatingInputSheet.tsx implements a bottom sheet with overlay, slide-in animation, rounded top corners, themed border/background, and visual language consistent with EventSheet.tsx.
RatingInputSheet fields include editable slot start/end, rating, efficiency, optional activity, optional mood, optional reflection, save, and cancel.
RatingInputSheet applies max lengths: mood 20, activity 50, reflection 200.
src/features/rating/components/RatingHistoryList.tsx groups items by date descending and renders each item as a themed card showing time slot, star rating, efficiency, and activity summary.
src/features/rating/copy/empty-state-quips.ts contains exactly the provided 50 quips and pickRandomQuip without additions, deletions, or wording changes.
Empty state chooses one quip only on mount using useMemo or lazy useState and displays an arrow or clear visual direction toward the FAB.
All new component colors come from useTheme; no direct color literals are introduced in rating UI components unless the existing theme system already requires transparent/system constants.
tests: Component-level smoke tests if the project already has React Native component test setup; otherwise skip UI tests as specified and rely on TypeScript plus manual verification.
Unit test or snapshot-like assertion for empty-state-quips.ts: array length is 50 and pickRandomQuip returns a member of the array.
Manual test checklist: StarRating press changes selected value and shows feedback.
Manual test checklist: EfficiencySlider snaps to 1-5 discrete values and displays current value.
Manual test checklist: RatingInputSheet opens/closes with animation and enforces field lengths.
Manual test checklist: History cards group by date and sort newest first.

phases.name: Rating Tab Integration
phases.description: Add the new RATING tab screen and wire the UI components to the service/hook. This phase makes the local feature usable from the main app navigation.
acceptance: app/rating.tsx displays rating history from useRatings and a right-bottom FAB for creating a new rating.
FAB opens RatingInputSheet with default time slot set to current time minus 1 hour through the service or screen orchestration.
Saving a rating closes the sheet and immediately updates the history list.
Killing and reopening the app still shows previously saved ratings from AsyncStorage.
History item press opens a read-only detail view or modal for v1; editing is not implemented.
app/_layout.tsx adds RATING as the fourth tab in order: TODAY, MATRIX, RATING, SETTINGS.
The RATING tab uses Star from lucide-react-native.
The RATING tab icon behavior, selected/unselected states, font sizing, colors, and transition pattern match existing TODAY/MATRIX/SETTINGS tabs.
Tab label typography uses Orbitron where existing tabs do.
No existing ScheduleEvent schema or import flow is modified.
tests: Manual navigation test: RATING appears between MATRIX and SETTINGS.
Manual persistence test: add one rating, force quit app, reopen, rating is still visible.
Manual empty-state test: fresh storage shows one stable random quip and FAB direction indicator.
Manual detail test: tapping a history card opens read-only details without edit affordances.
Run TypeScript/lint checks available in the project to catch navigation and prop type errors.

phases.name: JSON Export from Settings
phases.description: Add a settings action that exports all local rating records as JSON. Prefer expo-sharing if already installed; otherwise use React Native Share.share(string) as the fallback.
acceptance: Settings page includes a button labeled 导出打分数据.
Pressing the button loads all ratings through ratings.service.ts or the repository-backed public API, not ratings.storage.ts directly.
Exported JSON is valid JSON and contains the complete TimeSlotRating records including rating, efficiency, timestamps, schema_version, and synced_at when present.
If expo-sharing is installed and usable, export uses it; otherwise the implementation falls back to Share.share(string).
The export implementation is isolated enough that future cloud sync/export changes do not require rewriting storage.
tests: Unit test for export helper, if extracted: serializes an empty list to [] and records with optional fields/emoji/long strings without throwing.
Manual test: create at least one rating, tap 导出打分数据, open/share JSON, verify structure.
Manual fallback test or code-path inspection: Share.share fallback exists when expo-sharing is unavailable.
Run npm test to ensure storage and repository tests still pass.

phases.name: Documentation and Final Verification
phases.description: Update architecture documentation and run the full acceptance pass for the MVP. This phase closes gaps, verifies tests, and records the new feature structure and API contracts.
acceptance: ARCHITECTURE.md documents src/features/rating/ in the directory structure.
ARCHITECTURE.md data-flow section includes the rating branch: UI/hook -> ratings.service.ts -> RatingRepository -> LocalRatingRepository -> ratings.storage.ts -> AsyncStorage.
ARCHITECTURE.md API Contracts section lists rating service CRUD signatures and pending-sync/export-relevant behavior.
npm test passes, including ratings.storage.test.ts and local-repository.test.ts.
The app can run on a phone/APK build path without TypeScript or bundling errors.
Manual acceptance checklist is completed: add rating, kill process and reopen, see persisted rating, export JSON, verify JSON structure.
Any known limitations are documented: no cloud sync, no MCP endpoint, no widget, no AI summary, no edit flow in v1.
tests: Run npm test.
Run project TypeScript/lint command if available.
Run Expo app locally and verify rating tab flow manually.
Build or run APK validation command used by the project, if available.
Inspect ARCHITECTURE.md diff to confirm feature directory, data flow, and API contracts are present.
